title: @libs/gated-scoped-ac
subject: gated-scoped-ac
summary: Scoped access control as a library: an engine that turns a caller's permissions into scopes and verdicts, and a gated db that reaches the database only through them.

purpose.intro: The library behind [[access-control|Access Control]]. Rules are declared as config; for each request an engine turns the caller's permissions into a [[scope]] or a verdict, and the [[gated db]] reaches the database only with one. These pages are the library's reference: its surface, how an app wires it, how a slice calls it, and how it works inside.
points: **The engine** (`createAc`) resolves read, update and delete scopes and the create and update verdicts. It is pure: it builds drizzle SQL fragments and never holds a connection.
**The gate** (`createGatedDb`) owns the database handle. Its read, update and delete each take a scope of the matching entity and action, so a query that skips access control does not compile.
**The config loaders** (`definePermissions`, `registerPermissions`, `registerForests`) type and validate permissions and [[role forest|role forests]] when the config loads.
**The [[access context]]** (`ScopedAcRequestContext`) is the value an app builds once per request and every layer below reads.
purpose.note: The principles and their AC ids are in [[access-control|Access Control]]. These pages describe the code in `shared/libs/gated-scoped-ac/src`.

reference.statement: Everything is imported from `@libs/gated-scoped-ac`, the zod adapter from `@libs/gated-scoped-ac/zod`. The brand symbol that marks a scope is not exported.

reference.statement: One runtime dependency, one optional peer, and nothing from the app.

claims.text: `drizzle-orm` is the one runtime dependency: the engine builds drizzle `sql` fragments and the gate runs drizzle queries on the handle it is given.
`zod` is an optional peer, loaded only by `@libs/gated-scoped-ac/zod`. Importing the library's root never pulls it in.
No web framework, no auth provider and no app module: the app's middleware builds the [[access context]] and hands the library what it needs.

reference.statement: In reading order; each stands on its own.

claims.text: [[gated-scoped-ac-architecture|Architecture]]: which file owns what, what lives how long, how a request passes through.
[[gated-scoped-ac-dsl-rules|DSL rules]]: permissions, conditions, traversals and role forests as the loaders accept them.
[[gated-scoped-ac-bag|Access context]]: the bag, the permissions and the per-request handle, and how paths resolve against them.
[[gated-scoped-ac-mount|Mount]]: building the engine and the gate once, and the hydration that builds the context per request.
[[gated-scoped-ac-ac-patterns|AC patterns]]: what a service and a repository call for each of create, read, update and delete.
[[gated-scoped-ac-security|Security]]: what the library guarantees, and what it trusts the app with.
[[gated-scoped-ac-internals|Internals]]: how the engine compiles rules and how the gate assembles and runs them.
[[gated-scoped-ac-troubleshooting|Troubleshooting]]: the errors the library throws, and why a read comes back empty.

reference.statement: `shared/libs/gated-scoped-ac/test/` runs the real engine and gate against PGlite, with a fixture schema (organization, user, membership, note, note_share, note_comment and a view) and its own config.

claims.text: `behavior`: reads, writes and denials per persona. `operators`: the four operators on single-value, array and json columns. `traversal`: joins and the far-side column. `payload`: create rules on the row being written. `implied-roles`, `zod-adapter`, and `types.test-d.ts` for what must not compile.
Run them with `pnpm --dir shared/libs/gated-scoped-ac test`; the type tests with `test:types`.
